lab._comment: NO AUTHORITY. Part 7. Nothing in `verdicts` or `cues` may name anything in here; capart enforces it. A treatment leaves the lab by being MOVED into Parts 1-6, never by being cited from there. A new idea gets a `lab` key, an `asks`, and a section in Part 7. ⚠ ONE entry. `duration_band` (L7) was CLEARED 2026-08-27 — the ledger has the row: its cells had drifted out of agreement with its own `asks`, drawing the RemainingPercent route as though the question were still open after V19 promoted the seconds form. An entry whose cells no longer draw its question is decoration, which Part 7 says to delete rather than repair. `ring_collision` (L9) replaces it and is a LOOK question, not a capability one: every pixel in it is already shipped, so there is nothing to fly — what is unsettled is whether the composition reads as one statement or two.

ring_collision.title: L9 · ring_collision — a row that is IN the scan and RULED OUT at the same time
ring_collision.asks: Part 3 records this as an OPEN DESIGN QUESTION and Part 4 as a settled rule, and they do not agree. A row wearing a negative cue is `scan: true` — the verdicts carrying `blocked` all are — so it draws V13's yellow edge AND cap's half of V11's red hatch, which say opposite things about the same button. Today GEOMETRY keeps them apart rather than order: `hatch.skip.overhang_px` holds the red 2px OUTSIDE the icon rect, so the rings are adjacent at −2 and 0 and never overlap. Part 4 nonetheless asserts that an eliminating mark draws over an including one and that THE FRAME LEVEL SAYS SO — and neither `Paint.Border` nor `Paint.Hatch` calls `SetFrameLevel`, so nothing declares it and construction order decides. Drawn side by side: does the double ring read as ONE statement or two, and if two, is the answer the overlap (drop the overhang and let red cover yellow), suppression (no edge on a ruled-out row), or the adjacency we already have?

cells.caption: L9a · control — in the scan, nothing against it. V13's yellow edge alone, at the shipped 2px and alpha. This is what the red has to argue with; rule 2 says an entry needing a comparison draws its own control, since the declared style is no longer one scroll away.

L9b · control — ruled out with NO contradiction. `cd` is the one verdict that is `scan: false`, so V11's cooldown half draws and no edge competes with it. One statement, and the only ruled-out row in the vocabulary that gets to be unambiguous.

L9c · THE SUBJECT — both at once. Yellow edge (in the scan), red hatch with its own red border (ruled out), and the red `blocked` badge saying why. Three marks, two of which disagree. The badge is the only one carrying a REASON; the other two carry verdicts, and one of those verdicts is wrong about this row.

L9d · THE PROPOSAL — red covers yellow, and the yellow is never removed. Same row as L9c with two changes and no others: the skip ring's overhang drops to 0 so its opaque red border lands exactly on the icon rect where V13's yellow edge lives, and it is lifted above the edge so it actually covers it. The stripe fill goes to 0.85. ⚠ The scan edge is still drawn, in full, underneath — this is OCCLUSION, not suppression, which is the point: adding a texture over a line is cheap, and teaching `Treatment.For` to withhold the edge on a ruled-out row is not. If this reads, candidate 2 (suppression) never has to be built.

skip_overrides._comment: A lab cell may redraw V11's SKIP layer with its own geometry, WITHOUT touching `tokens.hatch.skip`. Only the keys an override names change; the hue, the stripe sheet and the phase stay the shelf's, so a cell is a question about ONE dimension rather than a second style. TWO lifts, and they are not the same job. `lift` raises the skip layer over V13's scan edge — the preview appends that edge AFTER the skip layer, so without it the yellow paints over the red no matter what the geometry says; it is the CSS stand-in for the `SetFrameLevel` Part 4 asserts and `Paint.lua` does not make. `chrome_lift` puts the BADGE and the HOTKEY back on top of both. Raising the hatch over the edge raises it over everything else drawn after it too, and a hatch that conceals the badge has eaten the only mark on the row carrying a REASON — which inverts what V11 is for. Measured on L9d 2026-08-27.

overlap._comment: The overhang STAYS at the shelf's 2 — the hatch reading slightly larger than the icon is the effect being kept, not the one under test. What covers the yellow is the BORDER WEIGHT: at 4px, drawn 2px outside the rect, the red band spans −2..+2 and swallows V13's 0..2 edge whole while still overhanging. Dropping the overhang to 0 also covers the edge and was tried first — it throws away the overhang to buy nothing the thicker border does not.
